name: use-travel-direction
title: useTravelDirection
description: Names which way a sliding indicator is travelling, so each of its edges can take its own easing.

files.content:
import * as React from 'react'

/**
 * Which way a sliding indicator is travelling, for the per-edge easing that
 * gives it its stretch (`.wj-segment-pill`, `.wj-nav-highlight`,
 * `.wj-toggle-knob` hardcodes its own pair because it has only two states).
 *
 * Derived from the item ORDER rather than the measured offset: the measurement
 * from `useSlidingIndicator` lands an effect later than the selection change,
 * so reading it would name the direction in the same commit that moves the
 * edges, or a commit too late. Adjusting state during render (React's
 * documented pattern) puts the value on the element one commit BEFORE the edges
 * move, which is what the transition needs.
 *
 * A ref here would be wrong -- StrictMode renders twice and the second pass
 * would compare the new index against itself.
 *
 * An index of -1 -- no selection, or an id that is not in the list -- is skipped
 * rather than recorded, so a selection that passes through nothing (a search
 * filtering every tab out and back) still travels from where it left.
 */
export function useTravelDirection(index: number): 'forward' | 'back' {
  const [previous, setPrevious] = React.useState(index)
  const [direction, setDirection] = React.useState<'forward' | 'back'>('forward')

  if (index !== -1 && previous !== index) {
    setDirection(index < previous ? 'back' : 'forward')
    setPrevious(index)
  }

  return direction
}

docs: Pair with useSlidingIndicator when an indicator is positioned by BOTH edges: the direction picks which edge leads, which is what gives the SegmentedControl pill and the HeaderNav / SidebarTabs highlights their stretch. Derived from the item order and adjusted during render, so the value is on the element one commit before the edges move -- reading the measured offset instead would name the direction a commit too late.
